question: What organ acts as the temporary lung and kidney for the developing foetus?
explanation: The placenta takes over the functions of gas exchange, nutrition, and waste elimination since the foetal organs are not yet active. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: Why is blood flow directed away from the lungs during intrauterine life?

options.A: The lungs are fluid-filled and have high vascular resistance
options.B: Deoxygenated blood is toxic to developing lung tissue
options.C: The right ventricle fails to pump blood during gestation
options.D: The pulmonary artery is completely absent until birth

explanation: High pulmonary vascular resistance causes blood to take paths of least resistance through specialized shunts rather than entering the unventilated lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h1)

question: What is the name of the shunt that connects the pulmonary artery directly to the descending aorta?
explanation: The ductus arteriosus diverts most pulmonary trunk blood directly into the systemic circulation, bypassing the lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: Which shunt allows blood to pass directly from the right atrium into the left atrium?
explanation: The foramen ovale is an opening in the atrial septum that shunts oxygenated blood entering the right side of the heart across to the left side. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: Which vessel carries oxygen-rich blood away from the placenta toward the foetus?
explanation: Despite carrying oxygenated blood, the umbilical vein is termed a vein because it transports blood toward the foetal heart. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of blood passing through the foramen ovale into the left side of the heart?

options.A: It warms the blood before it reaches the lungs
options.B: It filters out metabolic waste products before systemic distribution
options.C: It directs the most oxygenated blood toward the brain and heart
options.D: It relieves hydrostatic pressure within the right ventricle

explanation: The routing ensures vital upper body structures receive blood with the highest available oxygen content. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h3)

question: Which vessels transport deoxygenated blood from the foetus back to the placenta?
explanation: Two umbilical arteries carry metabolic waste and deoxygenated blood away from the foetal internal iliacs back to the placental chorionic villi. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: What happens to the majority of blood that enters the foetal pulmonary trunk?

options.A: It circulates through the alveoli for immediate gas exchange
options.B: It drains directly into the superior vena cava
options.C: It flows through the ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta
options.D: It pools in the right ventricle due to valve closure

explanation: High pulmonary vascular resistance forces blood away from the lungs and through the ductus arteriosus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h4)

question: What is the immediate mechanical effect of clamping the umbilical cord on systemic circulation?

options.C: Systemic blood pressure drops to zero

explanation: Removing the low-resistance placental circuit causes a sudden rise in systemic vascular resistance. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: Which physiological trigger is primarily responsible for the functional closure of the foramen ovale at birth?

options.A: The complete disappearance of umbilical arteries
options.B: A sudden decrease in circulating maternal hormones
options.C: Increased left atrial pressure relative to the right atrium

explanation: The sudden influx of blood from the newly expanded lungs raises left atrial pressure, pushing the septum primum against the septum secundum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h5)

question: What pharmacological agent is commonly used to maintain the patency of the ductus arteriosus in neonates with cyanotic heart defects?
explanation: Prostaglandin infusions relax the smooth muscle of the ductus arteriosus, keeping it open when systemic blood flow depends on it. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical consequence of a failure in normal foetal circulatory closure?

options.A: Cyanosis when shunting reverses in congenital anomalies
options.B: Permanent closure of all cardiac valves before birth
options.C: Increased pulmonary blood flow in patent ductus arteriosus
options.D: Left-to-right blood shunting through persistent structures

explanation: Valves do not close permanently before birth due to failure of shunts; rather, specific shunts like the ductus arteriosus or foramen ovale fail to close after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h6)
